name: BSP_SizedStoragePool_AllocateBlock
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Packet app_init_alloc_string_helpers, assembly-verified. __thiscall, ECX string pool (00419cc0), stack (uint size, uint unused), RET 8; the second argument is never read. size >= 0x96 goes straight to _malloc 00bf9f1a. Otherwise, under the lock at this+0x8ad484: if head[size] == (tail[size]+1) & 0x7ffff the free ring region for that size is empty and a block is carved off the bump arena at this+8, advancing the offset at this+0x6acfc8 by the EXACT byte count with no alignment and no bounds check of any kind. Otherwise the live count at ring+0x2004b0 is decremented and ring[tail[size]] is popped, tail[size] -= 1 modulo the ring. Size classes are indexed by byte size, so a block is only ever reused for a request of exactly the same size. Evidence: docs/APP_INIT_ALLOC_STRINGS.md.

name: BSP_GameAllocator_AllocateBlock
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Packet app_init_alloc_string_helpers, assembly-verified. __thiscall, ECX game pool, stack (uint size), RET 4. size >= 0x81 goes to _malloc 00bf9f1a. Otherwise under the lock at this+0xb89a98: pop ring[tail[size]] for that exact size, or, when head[size] == (tail[size]+1) & 0x7ffff marks the region empty, carve from the bump arena at this+0x200414 and advance the offset at this+0xb89a94 by (size+3) & ~3. Unlike the string pool this rounds the carve up to four bytes; like it, there is no arena bounds check. Evidence: docs/APP_INIT_ALLOC_STRINGS.md.

name: BSP_SizedStoragePool_ReturnSmallBlock
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Packet app_init_alloc_string_helpers, assembly-verified; drops the _Provisional suffix. __thiscall, ECX the free-ring subobject (pool+0x6acfcc for the string pool, pool+4 for the game pool), stack (void** block, uint size_class), RET 8; the block is read through the pointer and never written back. Ring layout: 0x80000 pointer slots at +0, head[] at +0x200000, tail[] one class array later (+0x200258 for 150 classes, +0x200204 for 129), then the live count and the high-water mark. Each size class owns a contiguous circular slice laid down by the constructor as head[i] = i*stride (0xda7 string pool, 0xfe0 game pool), tail[i] = head[i]-1. Push advances the class's own tail; if that collides with the head of the next class, that class's whole region rotates forward one slot and its first element is displaced into the vacated slot, becoming the block that still needs a home, cascading until a class with slack is found or the walk wraps back to the starting class. Finally ring[tail[last]] takes the carried block, the live count rises and the high-water mark follows it. Evidence: docs/APP_INIT_ALLOC_STRINGS.md.

Sized release: size >= 0x96 goes to _free 00bf9dc8, otherwise, and only while DAT_01090aa4 is zero, the block is pushed onto the free ring for that EXACT size by 00bd12a0 (ECX = pool+0x6acfcc, args &block and size) under the lock at pool+0x8ad484. A non-zero DAT_01090aa4 drops the block instead of freeing it. The size must be the size the block was allocated with, because it selects the free list. 2851 callers.
